title: BREAKING: ICE Raids Home Depot in California-Ignores Gavin Newsom's Sanctuary Screeching (VIDEO)
text:
In a bold move that’s already making waves across California, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents conducted a major raid at a Home Depot near Los Angeles—sending a clear message to Governor Gavin Newsom and Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass: federal law still matters.
The raid, captured on video and confirmed by multiple eyewitnesses, unfolded swiftly at the store’s parking lot. Agents reportedly apprehended several individuals suspected of being in the country illegally, drawing cheers from immigration enforcement advocates and outrage from the state’s pro-sanctuary leadership.
News of the operation was first shared by Fox News’ Matt Finn and amplified by independent journalist Nick Sortor, who pointed out that ICE is “IGNORING Gavin Newsom and Karen Bass’ whining.” For years, California’s sanctuary policies have provided cover for illegal immigrants—even those with criminal records—by limiting cooperation with federal enforcement.
Watch the moment here:
https://www.usasupreme.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/ice.mp4 https://www.usasupreme.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/homedepot.mp4 But that may be changing.
While Newsom has repeatedly vowed to shield illegal immigrants from deportation, ICE’s unannounced presence at a popular retail location shows that federal authorities are no longer playing by California’s woke rules.
As expected, pro-illegal immigration activists are fuming. But many ordinary citizens in the area were seen filming and even applauding the operation. With California reeling from rising crime, housing shortages, and out-of-control costs of living—much of it worsened by illegal immigration—public sentiment is clearly shifting.
The footage circulating online has gone viral, sparking debate over state vs. federal authority and whether more raids could be coming. One thing is clear: ICE isn’t waiting for Newsom’s permission—and Californians might finally be seeing some long-overdue enforcement.
